newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Restructure drives Electrolux to H1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Restructure drives Electrolux to H1 loss.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux on Wednesday posted a loss of 264 million crowns ($32.6 million) for the first half of 1997 due to hefty restructuring costs of 2.5 billion crowns charged against the second quarter.
The market had expected a loss of 305 million crowns.
Electrolux said sales in the six months to June 30 were flat at 57.27 billion crowns against 57.01 billion crowns a year ago when it posted a profit of 1.81 billion crowns.

Chief executive Michael Treschow, who initiated the tough restructuring drive in June, said the second quarter of the year had seen some improvements and better markets for white goods, especially in North America.
Even so, operating income from the group's white goods division fell over the period.

Treschow said higher sales in several European countries had contributed to an increase of five percent in total group sales for comparable units after adjustment for exchange rate effects in the second quarter.
He also said white goods demand in the U.S. had been at high levels in most product areas this year, with the exception of room air conditioners.
"Despite lower volumes in this area, results for the American white goods operation continued to improve," Treschow said in the results statement.
But disappointments in the second quarter included trends for white goods in Brazil and in Europe, where continued difficult market conditions in Germany had an impact.
German sales account for almost 30 percent of white goods sales in Europe.
"In both Germany and the rest of Europe, we must reduce cost levels and increase productivity, which is the aim of the recently authorised restructuring programme," Treschow said.
He said 1,500 jobs would be cut in Germany in 1998 as part of a plan to axe 12,000 jobs worldwide.
Lower demand was behind the trend in Brazil but Treschow said he expected a recovery in the second half of the year.

Total operating income for white goods was lower than in 1996 for both the half year and the second quarter. For the six months it fell to 1.15 billion crowns from 1.20 billion crowns, although sales rose about 10 percent to 39.76 billion crowns.

Operating income from Electrolux's commercial appliances division improved in the second quarter to 134 million crowns from 116 million a year earlier, while the outdoor products area saw continued strong sales and income trends.

Discounting restructuring costs and a capital gain of 604 million crowns from the sale of Husqvarna Sewing Machines, Treschow said the group's pre-tax income for comparable units was on a level with the previous year.
"The group has shown weak profitability for some time," Treschow said, with operating margins of 4.1 percent in the first half against a target of 6.5-7.0 percent.
"Both operating margin and return on equity have been far from the established long-term goals."
Electrolux share price fell on the report and was trading eight crowns lower at 607 at 1230 GMT. By 1300 GMT the share was trading at 617, up two crowns on Tuesday's close.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1045
($ = 8.106 Swedish Crowns)
